criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Identifies GBR coral monitoring, users, need and references, but objectives and design requirements such as resolution, revisit, latency, coverage and data products are not quantified or complete.

evidence.quote: would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events.
report sea surface temperatures, thermal stress on coral, and bathymetry

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Gantt/timetable with task details and deadlines; information sources are listed. However there is no explicit contingency or variation planning and limited direct linkage to mission technical drivers, so the plan is feasible but not robust.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Only background reading and completion of STK tutorials are reported; no design calculations, trade studies or simulation outputs. This is minor useful progress, not preliminary technical results.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear headings and readable prose; the Gantt is legible but lacks a figure caption/number. Footnotes support the first section, but the Useful Links are uncited and reference formatting is inconsistent.

technical_issues.issue: No measurable mission/design requirements are given: orbit, revisit, spatial/spectral resolution, latency, coverage, data rate and payload are undefined.
Assumes satellite detection of seafloor colour/tone changes using an Asner-style system without water-column, atmospheric-correction or sensor-resolution feasibility trade.
No actual STK results or launch/orbit calculations are presented; tutorial completion is not design evidence.
Ground-control statement that one station may suffice for Australia ignores coverage, contact duration and near-real-time latency requirements.
End-of-life option 'leaving it where it is' is not compliant with space-debris mitigation; deorbit or graveyard orbit must match the chosen orbit.
The plan lacks contingency allowance and does not explicitly confirm STK licensing/software arrangements.

overall: A readable preliminary concept with clear GBR rationale, users, Gantt plan and sources, but weak on formal requirements, mission-design calculations and actual STK results. It meets the concept and planning brief adequately; technical progress and presentation need strengthening.

feedback.summary: Your preliminary report presents a clear GBR coral-monitoring concept with users, rationale and sources, and a readable Gantt-based plan. To reach the next level, quantify mission and design requirements, add contingency and software/licensing detail, and show actual STK/design results rather than tutorial completion. Presentation also needs a captioned Gantt and consistent citations.
next_steps: In Mission Concept & Rationale, convert goals into measurable requirements (orbit, revisit, spatial/spectral resolution, latency, coverage, data rate, payload) and add a short feasibility trade on water-column/atmospheric correction and sensor resolution for seafloor colour detection.

In Project Plan & Preliminary Progress, add explicit contingency/variation allowance, confirm STK licensing arrangements, and replace tutorial-completion evidence with actual STK outputs or launch/orbit calculations; revisit the single-ground-station assumption and end-of-life option against debris mitigation.
In presentation, add a numbered caption to Image 1 (Gantt), cite or remove the Useful Links entries, and align in-text citations with the reference list; use consistent figure/table formatting.

criteria.C1: You clearly identify GBR coral monitoring, users and need, with references. The next level requires quantified objectives and design requirements: orbit, revisit, spatial/spectral resolution, latency, coverage, data rate and payload. Also justify seafloor colour detection with a water-column, atmospheric-correction and sensor-resolution feasibility trade rather than assuming an Asner-style system will work.
criteria.C2: Your Gantt/timetable and listed sources make the plan credible. To move from Adequate to Accomplished, add explicit contingency and variation planning, show how tasks link to mission technical drivers, and confirm STK licensing/software arrangements. The plan should explain why it is structured this way for this mission, not just list weekly tasks.
criteria.C3: You report background reading and STK tutorials 1–4, which is useful but not preliminary design evidence. The next level needs actual results: STK outputs, launch/orbit calculations, trade studies or simulation plots with brief interpretation. Also address the single-ground-station coverage/latency assumption and replace 'leaving it where it is' with a debris-compliant deorbit or graveyard option.
criteria.C4: Your headings and prose are readable, and the Gantt is legible. To reach Accomplished, add a numbered caption to Image 1, cite or remove the Useful Links entries, and make in-text citations match the reference list consistently. Check figure/table formatting and language style throughout so the document reads professionally.
